idea: an arrow drawn from a source edge into a target edge, its head appearing only as the shaft arrives
outline: kit.arrow shaft path between two edge points (optionally bent)
m.draw of the shaft at a cue
arrowhead opacity 0 -> 1 in the last moment of the draw
variation_seen: b16: two straight vertical arrows, bubble bottom to card top, sw 5, colour per yield, default head
b19: one horizontal arrow sw 8 head 34 in a dim wrapper, hand-rolled dasharray so it can later UN-draw back to its source, plus a label unmasked with the stroke
b20: three diagonal arrows computed edge-to-edge between rectangles, sw 6 head 28, later pulsed together (shaft width and head scale)

future_uses.shows: an arrow from a supplier node into a warehouse node
arrows carrying light and CO2 into a leaf
an arrow from one stage card into the next

reason: The form is already the engine's own primitives: kit.arrow returns {g, path, head} and every use is kit.arrow + m.draw(a.path) + a one-line head fade, the same idiom the shipped core.js flow template uses, so a component would wrap three lines and carry no on-screen content; the parts that actually varied (edge-to-edge geometry in b20, un-draw retraction with a dim wrapper and label in b19, pulse emphasis in b20) are each scene's bespoke choreography and would not fit one param set. All three uses are from one lesson; if the head-lands-late timing is worth centralising, it belongs as an option on the motion primitive (for example m.draw recognising a kit.arrow result and landing its head at the end), not as a library component.
